already_exposed_prior_publication: Cox et al 2024 10.1007/s00300-024-03246-9, direct nest success and 2022 reoccupancy, 4 nascent subcolonies already described
screen_question: Within solitary nest territories, does gain of a neighbor recorded in November (before median late December hatch) co-occur with more directly CONFIRMED chicks entering creches? Does this pattern survive earlier/later exposure cutoff description?
eligible: Only 2021 nests whose original breeder=1, excluding solo27 (author's stated inadequate observations); expect 36
neighbor_definition: Any original raw n_neighbors >0 on dated 2021 observation at or before cutoff; finite numeric 0 is absence; do not infer actual conspecific arrival date from first positive
outcome: cr_confirm >0 means directly confirmed at least one chick entering creche; 0/NA means NOT DIRECTLY CONFIRMED, not certain death
checks: exact source 50 GPS positions and 50 unique outcome IDs
only before median hatch cutoff dates
no row after cutoff may influence exposure
exposure groups minimum n reported with each date, no arbitrary significance gate
report balance at baseline and site/area clustering; no p value or inferred causality
detect observer and eggs already present at first neighbor appearance as a reverse-causation warning
mechanisms_unresolved: social protection via new near neighbors
selective persistence of successful early breeders attracts neighbors
local microtopography/skua predator risk and surveillance affect both neighbors and chick observation
egg/nest attendance encourages settlement prior to chick success
site grouping and reuse may be identity-confounded
claim_not_licensed: neighbors caused chick survival or founded new colony, evolution of Allee threshold, independent first-recruitment or island-scale causal regularity
